summary: No reachable vulnerability. (1) Stored text: explanation, chart line, equity strings and opponent lines ('name: basis') reach the DOM only as React text children / template-literal text in src/ui/table/ReviewPanel.tsx; no dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML anywhere in src/. data-opponent is a numeric seat attribute. So even a hand-crafted IndexedDB record could not inject markup. (2) Worker grade replies: the worker is the app's own same-origin bundle (advice.worker.ts -> handleAdviceRequest, which already accepted 'observed' for grade); it is not a trust boundary. decisionEntry copies the reply without shape-checking it, but records are validated by parseHandRecord when read back, and a malformed reply that makes storedReviewEntries/handWrite throw rejects the write promise and is logged, so it fails closed: no panel entries, no record. No untrusted path reaches that code, so I'm not raising a finding. (3) Opponent hole-card leakage: review entries are built from hand.userDecisions[i].view, a PlayerView. playerView copies fields by name and exposes only the viewer's holeCards (PublicPlayer has none). opponentLines uses only seat, folded and the stored basis text. Observed stats come from userObservedSnapshot/earlierShowdowns, which carry only shown hands. The review adds no opponent cards. (4) No new dependencies, no network, no randomness, no secrets, no file or temp handling. The e2e ten-seat-review scene lives under e2e/support and is not in the production bundle.
